add: Plain packages (SOT, SOIC, QFN, SOD, chip and every other part that is not a module): never use the module family for them. Find the starter row with library_templates (for example "sot-23 pins:5"); each result has a starter name and its values. Plan and build with request {"draft": <the package draft id>, "row": {"source": "starter", "name": <starter name>}, "values": <that row's values, each corrected from the mechanical drawing>}. values keep exactly the row's fields and its family; library_package_schema describes only the module family, so don't call it for a plain package.

The tabbed family (SOT-23, SOT-223, DPAK) takes the datasheet's land pattern in values: "lands": {"size": [land width across the lead, land length], "span": the two rows' land centre to land centre}. Set it from the recommended land pattern whenever the datasheet has one: the row's own lands are estimates. Check the built footprint once with library_inspect_draft.

The row is exactly {"source": "starter", "name": ...} with no other field. In a tabbed form, span is the leads' tip-to-tip span of the package (not the land span), and each lead needs room to bend down outside the body: (span − body_width) / 2 − foot_length must exceed lead_thickness. When the drawing gives a range, take the nominal or the middle and say so in the report.

Don't use library_edit for descriptions, provenance or other wording: the review report is where sources and notes go. Use it only for a value the forms can't set, and then send the definition exactly as library_inspect_draft returned it with only that value changed. A marking text item is {"item": "text", "template": "<the marking>"}.
